acceptedAnswer.text: Planning, a custom theme, plugin selection or development, forms and tracking, speed work, security setup, migration and a handover guide. Scope is agreed in writing before work starts.

mainEntity.name: Do you use ready-made themes or build custom?

acceptedAnswer.text: We build custom themes to your design. We may use a lightweight starter framework underneath, but the design, templates and blocks are made for your brand.

mainEntity.name: Can you build a WooCommerce store?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We set up the catalogue, cart, checkout, payments, shipping and tax settings. If your catalogue is large or complex we will tell you if Shopify would serve you better.

mainEntity.name: Can you speed up my existing WordPress site?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes. We audit images, scripts, plugins, caching and hosting, then fix what is slowing pages down. We report what changed and what the site now loads like.

mainEntity.name: Can you migrate my site to WordPress?

acceptedAnswer.text: From other builders, older CMSs or another host, yes. We map URLs, set redirects and check the pages after the move so search visibility is protected.

mainEntity.name: Who maintains the site after launch?

acceptedAnswer.text: You can maintain it in-house with our editing guide, or we can run it under a monthly plan. See our website maintenance page for what that covers.

mainEntity.name: What does a WordPress site cost?

acceptedAnswer.text: It depends on pages, features and integrations. We scope it on a call and write the scope down, so you can compare it with other quotes.

answer.label: In short
answer.lead: WordPress development is the work of building and extending a site on WordPress: a custom theme, the right plugins, WooCommerce if you sell online, and the speed and security setup behind them. Done well, your team edits pages freely and the site stays fast.

paras: A WordPress site is more than a theme. It is the theme, the plugins, the hosting, the editing experience and the update routine. We plan all five before we write code, so the site is easy to run after launch.

For stores we build on WooCommerce when the catalogue and checkout are simple enough to live on WordPress, and recommend Shopify when they are not. You get a straight recommendation, not whichever platform we prefer.
